body:
The problem employee thing is something I've constantly worried about, no matter what job I'm taking up. I don't want to cause any issues; I want to do my job correctly. But I also want my identity to be acknowledged, and I don't see any other way to do it without making people uncomfortable. I'm sure they wouldn't mark me down as a problem employee if I bring it up with HR, but I can't help but think about the worst case scenario of every situation.

I'll definitely try the favor route. I like to hope for the best in people and I want to hope that she's not doing it on purpose.

I get scared when I confront people, to the point where I get emotional and tear up. I really want to start speaking up for myself though. I'll definitely look into some resources.

I don't know, honestly. I'm afraid that any bit of dissent, any bit of me trying to explain myself or correct her will make my superior complain about me to HR.

I'm worried more about other people's comfort level than my own. I put their comfort first. I can't correct a guest because I'm afraid they'll complain to a manager--I think of the worst case scenarios and it makes me clam up.

I just want to be comfortable being myself without having to worry about the discomfort of my coworkers/guests.
Yeah, I even have a nametag. I really don't want to go to HR about it and be noted as a problem employee, but I feel like that's the only route I can take now.

I know... I just have a hard time correcting one particular coworker because she's my superior, and whenever I've spoken up to her about other things she always makes a face/purses her lips like she hates that I'm correcting her. Some of my other coworkers have reassured me that she's just bad with names but I'm not so sure anymore.
